title: Explain and apply procedures pertaining to restricted areas at a race course on race day

lessons.title: Restricted areas and why they exist
lessons.html:
What is a restricted area?

On race day a racecourse has public areas, such as the grandstands and restaurants, and restricted areas where only authorised people may go. Restricted areas protect the horses, the jockeys and the honesty of the racing. In South Africa racing is controlled by the National Horseracing Authority (NHA), and the racecourse operator and the NHA set the access rules.

Why access is controlled

  • Integrity: to stop anyone interfering with a horse, for example giving it a prohibited substance, before a race.
  • Safety: racehorses are fit, excited and can kick or bolt; crowds near them are dangerous.
  • Order: officials, jockeys and grooms must be able to work without disturbance.

Typical restricted areas

AreaWhat happens there
Racecourse stables (raceday stables)Horses are kept between arrival and their race
Saddling enclosure / saddling boxesTrainers and grooms saddle horses
Parade ringHorses are led around before the race so the public and officials can see them
Weighing room and jockeys' roomJockeys weigh out and in, change and wait
Track and track entrancesHorses go out to race and return
Testing (sampling) stableOfficials take samples for drug testing
Veterinary areaRacecourse vets examine horses

Who may enter

Usually only people with the right accreditation or licence: trainers, licensed grooms and stable staff, jockeys, officials, vets, farriers on duty and security. Each person may enter only the areas their card or badge allows. A groom's card does not give access to the jockeys' room, for example.

Your identification

Carry your groom's identity card or accreditation at all times on race day, and show it when asked. Never lend it to anyone. If it is lost, report it at once to your trainer.

lessons.title: Following procedures on race day
lessons.html:
Arriving and entering

  1. Arrive at the stable entrance and present your identification to security.
  2. The horse's identity may be checked against its documents or microchip by officials.
  3. Go to the stable you are allocated. Do not swap stables without permission.
  4. Bags and equipment may be searched. Co-operate politely.

In the raceday stables

  • Stay with your horse or make sure it is supervised as the rules require.
  • Do not let unauthorised people near your horse, including owners' friends, unless the rules and the trainer allow.
  • Do not give the horse any substance, feed, water additive or injection unless you are certain it is allowed and the trainer instructs it. Prohibited substances can lead to disqualification and penalties.
  • Keep the stable area tidy and do not smoke near bedding.

Saddling and the parade ring

Bring the horse to the saddling area at the time set. After saddling, lead the horse to the parade ring. In the parade ring, lead on the correct side, keep moving in the set direction, and keep a safe distance. Only authorised people (trainer, owner where allowed, jockey, officials) enter the ring. Follow the instructions of the ring steward.

Going to and from the track

Follow the route set by officials. Release the horse to the jockey at the point the rules say. Wait at the place where horses return. After the race, take the horse back by the set route.

Testing

If your horse is selected for sampling, go with it directly to the testing stable. Do not let anyone else handle it on the way. Stay with the horse while the official takes the sample and sign the forms as required. Do not leave until you are told the process is finished.

Behaviour

  • No alcohol or drugs on duty.
  • Be polite to officials and security; follow their instructions.
  • Do not place bets if the rules for stable staff prohibit it; ask your trainer.
  • Report anything suspicious, such as a stranger near the horses, to security or an official.

Breaking the rules can lead to fines, suspension of your licence, and the horse being disqualified.

Key points

  • Restricted areas protect integrity, safety and order on race day.
  • Carry and show your identification; never lend it.
  • Enter only areas your accreditation allows.
  • Never give a horse any substance without being sure it is allowed and instructed.
  • If selected for testing, stay with the horse until the process is complete.
